description: Number of moles equals mass divided by molar mass.
Molarity equals number of moles divided by volume in litres.
Density equals mass divided by volume.
The ideal gas law relates pressure, volume, amount, temperature, and gas constant.
pH is the negative base-10 logarithm of hydrogen ion concentration.
pOH is the negative base-10 logarithm of hydroxide ion concentration.
At 25 degrees Celsius, pH and pOH add up to 14.
Percentage yield compares actual yield with theoretical yield.
Mole fraction equals moles of a component divided by total moles.
Gas density can be calculated from pressure, molar mass, gas constant, and temperature.
Heat transferred equals mass times specific heat capacity times temperature change.
Enthalpy change equals enthalpy of products minus enthalpy of reactants.
Gibbs free energy change relates enthalpy, temperature, and entropy changes.
The equilibrium constant is expressed using equilibrium concentrations.
A general rate law relates reaction rate to reactant concentrations.
For a first-order reaction, half-life equals 0.693 divided by the rate constant.
The Nernst equation relates cell potential to standard potential and reaction quotient at 25 degrees Celsius.
Electrical charge equals number of moles of electrons multiplied by Faraday's constant.
Absorbance equals molar absorptivity times path length times concentration.
The dilution equation relates initial and final concentrations and volumes.
